advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm a `# nested-pytest-ok: <reason>` occurring inside a string element of the argv (not as a real comment) within the launch span cannot falsely excuse a genuine launch, or accept this as a known guard limitation.
evidence: tests/unit/test_nested_pytest_uniqueness.py:55-59 builds `marked` from `body = source.splitlines()` matching `_ESCAPE_MARKER in line`, a text scan independent of AST node identity

tests/unit/test_nested_pytest_uniqueness.py:63-67 excuses a launch when `marked.intersection(range(start, end + 1))` is non-empty — any span line bearing the marker text, including one inside a quoted argv element, suffices
advisory.finding: The escape-marker excuse is decided by a raw line-text scan (splitlines) over the whole literal span, not by AST, so marker text that appears inside a string element of the argv (or any comment) on any line within the launch literal's span will silently excuse the launch. Widening the match from the bracket line to the full span enlarges this false-negative surface.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a case asserting a `# nested-pytest-ok: <reason>` marker placed OUTSIDE a launch literal's line span (above the opening bracket or below the closing bracket) does NOT excuse the launch, pinning the range(start, end+1) boundary.
evidence: Production change under test: `if not marked.intersection(range(start, end + 1))` (tests/unit/test_nested_pytest_uniqueness.py:66)

The only new test places the marker on the 'pytest' element line: `"        'pytest',{marker}\n"` with `range` start at the `[` line 3 (tests/unit/test_nested_pytest_uniqueness.py:106,111) — mid-span, never on the start line, the closing-bracket end line, or outside the span.

ABSENCE: no assertion that a marker on a line above the opening bracket (e.g. the `subprocess.run(` line) or below the closing bracket is NOT counted as excusing the launch; a mutant such as `range(start - 1, end + 2)` would pass every existing assertion, so the guard's over-match boundary is regression-blind.
advisory.finding: The new whole-span marker match (range(start, end+1)) is only exercised with a marker mid-span; no test asserts that a marker OUTSIDE a launch's span fails to excuse it, so an over-widened span (the characteristic failure mode of this change) would go undetected.
advisory.suggested_fix: Extend test_a_marker_inside_a_black_split_launch_excuses_it (or add a sibling) that writes the marker on the `subprocess.run(` line preceding the bracket and asserts `_unmarked_launches(offender) == [3]`, and a case with the marker on the closing-bracket `end` line asserting `== []`.
